component: Public Flow spatial normalized-length, perpendicular-frame and tolerance-classification diagnostics
implementation: Extend the existing bounded Flow SDK probe with optional normalized-length queries, single/batch frames, fractional length tolerances and curve classification. A dependency-free Python report compares authored dense Bezier witnesses to public query outputs, validates complete orthonormal frames and preserves mismatches explicitly. The shared precise arc-length sampler and registered spatial-command guard remain unchanged.

native_capture.method: Owned private display, public RhinoCommon FlowSpaceMorph, NormalizedLengthParameter, FrameAt, PerpendicularFrameAt, GetPerpendicularFrames, IsLinear and TryGetPlane. No proprietary implementation inspected.
native_capture.note: Final six-case capture extends an earlier four-case discovery with fractional tolerance and classification queries. All four earlier SDK maps were reproduced exactly; scale-small and scale-0-01 describe the same authored geometry/points. The retained six SDK maps also exactly reproduce their original Flow frames/equivalence/precision captures. Diagnostic length queries are opt-in and preserve existing probe output when absent.

findings.interpretation: A constant initial-roll correction of the public perpendicular frames does not reproduce the dense spatial map at corresponding normalized lengths. Precise public length lookup and the four sampled fractional length tolerances also fail to reproduce Flow centers. Public plane classifications at tolerance 0.1 explain two small-scale initial frames; this does not establish the complete spatial mapping rule.

checks.command: python3 -m unittest tools.rhino_oracle.test_flow_spatial tools.rhino_oracle.test_flow_capture tools.rhino_oracle.test_flow_line tools.rhino_oracle.test_flow_grips

limitations: No new native spatial parity or production-kernel behavior is claimed. Eight original spatial point-map mismatches remain unresolved.
Public frame comparisons use corresponding normalized lengths. Flow position differences mean they are not evaluated at identical target parameters away from endpoints.
The tolerance-0.1 classification is a candidate rule supported at two initial frames; further geometries, directions and positions must qualify any production change.
No performance, GUI appearance or complete-workspace test claim.
